hints: Focus on what percentage by mass really means, the mass of sodium in one mole divided by the total molar mass.
Start by writing the correct formula for each compound, remembering that carbonate is $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ and oxide is $\text{O}^{2-}$, so both need two sodiums.
Work out $\frac{\text{mass of Na}}{M_r} \times 100$ for each, using $\text{Na}=23$, and look for the one that gives about three quarters sodium.
walkthrough:
**Recall the percentage by mass rule**

Great, this is a composition calculation. The trick is to compare how heavy the sodium part is against the whole compound.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\% \text{ by mass of Na} = \frac{\text{total mass of Na in formula}}{M_r \text{ of compound}} \times 100$$

**Write formulas and find $M_r$ values**

Let's get organised. Use $\text{Na}=23$, $\text{C}=12$, $\text{O}=16$, $\text{H}=1$, $\text{Cl}=35.5$.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$M_r(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3) = (2 \times 23) + 12 + (3 \times 16) = 106$$
$$M_r(\text{NaCl}) = 23 + 35.5 = 58.5$$
$$M_r(\text{NaOH}) = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40$$
$$M_r(\text{Na}_2\text{O}) = (2 \times 23) + 16 = 62$$

**Calculate % Na and pick the match**

Now divide the sodium mass by each $M_r$. Sodium oxide has the lightest partner (just one oxygen), so its % will be highest.

Chemical equation or calculation rule if applicable:
$$\% \text{Na in Na}_2\text{O} = \frac{46}{62} \times 100 = 74.2\%$$
For comparison, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ gives $43.4\%$, $\text{NaCl}$ gives $39.3\%$, and $\text{NaOH}$ gives $57.5\%$. Only sodium oxide matches 74.2%.

options.A: Incorrect. For $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$, $M_r = 106$ and mass of Na $= 46$, so % Na $= 46/106 \times 100 = 43.4\%$. The heavy carbonate ion dilutes the sodium percentage.
options.B: Incorrect. For $\text{NaCl}$, $M_r = 58.5$ and mass of Na $= 23$, so % Na $= 23/58.5 \times 100 = 39.3\%$. Students sometimes forget to use 35.5 for Cl, but even with rounding it is far below 74.2%.
options.C: Incorrect. For $\text{NaOH}$, $M_r = 40$ and mass of Na $= 23$, so % Na $= 23/40 \times 100 = 57.5\%$. This is the second highest, but the hydroxide group is still heavier than a single oxygen shared between two sodiums.
options.D: Correct. For $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $M_r = 62$ and mass of Na $= 46$, so % Na $= 46/62 \times 100 = 74.2\%$. Two light sodium atoms combined with only one light oxygen atom gives a very high sodium content.
